sources.note: The only other document on Nteng (66 pp., SIL Nigeria survey with wordlist); if any remark on stress/prosody exists for Nteng it would be here, though as a sociolinguistic survey it most likely has none. sources.citation: Blench, Roger & Michael Bulkaam. 2019. Nteng, an undocumented Chadic language of Central Nigeria. Circulation draft dated 20 Oct 2019, 24 pp. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation (rogerblench.info; downloaded via the Internet Archive).
sources.note: Nothing. Section 3 Phonology (pp. 4-6) treats vowels (length contrast), consonants (plain, palatalised, labialised) and 3.3 Tones (three phonetic tones L/M/H plus a rising Mid-High; High never in isolation, so underlying two heights). The words 'stress' and 'accent' do not occur anywhere in the 24 pages; the rest is a ~500-item wordlist with tone-marked IPA and lexical comparison.
